title: Canonical geometric orientation comparison equations
statement: Fix the spaces and operations of a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum]. For a coefficient stage with category $B_X$, tensor $\otimes_X$, coefficient lines $T_{X,d}$ and support adjunctions $f_!\dashv f^!$, twist coordinates are $f^*T_{Y,d}\cong T_{X,d}$, $T_{X,d}\otimes T_{X,e}\cong T_{X,d+e}$ and the coefficient unitor. Exchange coordinates are the A3 projection isomorphism on $(\omega_f,T_{Y,d})$ and A2 compact-support exchange on $\omega_f=f^!T_{Y,0}$. Define $\theta_{f,d}:\omega_f\otimes f^*T_{Y,d}\to f^!T_{Y,d}$ as the counit transpose of inverse projection followed by $\varepsilon_f\otimes1$ and the unitor. Define $\beta:u^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ as the transpose under $f'_!\dashv f'^!$ of $f'_!u^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ex}_!^{-1}}v^*f_!\omega_f\xrightarrow{v^*\varepsilon_f}v^*T_{Y,0}\cong T_{Y',0}$; thus its actual type is $u^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$. A geometric family consists of $\gamma_f:T_{X,d}\cong\omega_f$ for smooth separated finite-type $f$ of pure dimension $d\ge0$, independent of compactification, satisfying $\gamma_{f'}=\beta\,u^*\gamma_f\,c^{-1}$ for every separated finite-type base change and $\gamma_{gf}=\alpha^{-1}f^!(\gamma_g)\theta_{f,e}(\gamma_f\otimes1)(1\otimes c^{-1})p^{-1}$ for smooth composites. Here $\alpha$ is the adjunction mate of compact-support composition and $p$ is twist multiplication. For a supplied A5 comparison $C$, image coordinates use its monoidal and pullback comparisons, and compatibility means $w_C C(\gamma_f)=\gamma'_f t_C$. The coordinates are required to equal the given operations when used in the full family; they do not assert purity or existence. At ordinary etale finite coefficients the twist coordinates use the shifted root line, its derived pullback and tensor product from [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], with the single-complex and even-shift comparisons; the rank-one flatness property justifies the derived single-tensor computation. Exchange coordinates are needed only for the smooth morphisms occurring in the family and separated finite-type base changes. The ordinary etale shifted line comparisons are supplied by [def-sf-orientation-etale-line-comparisons].
